title: Technical Funds & Traders
html:
Funds that trade price, not fundamentals

These are mostly systematic trend-followers (also called CTAs or managed futures). They use computer rules built on price — moving averages, breakouts, momentum — across stocks, bonds, currencies and commodities.

FundApproachWhy it matters
Man AHLSystematic trend-following, one of the oldest and largestThe industry benchmark for computer-driven trend trading
TranstrendPure trend-following (Dutch)Known for sticking with trends through long cycles
Aspect CapitalSystematic trend-followingStays "true to trend" rather than diluting the strategy
Campbell & CoSystematic trend and multi-strategyDecades-long track record
Graham CapitalTrend plus discretionary macroMixes rules with human judgment
MillburnSystematic, multi-factorAdds machine learning to trend signals
Dunn CapitalPure, high-volatility trend-followingHuge swings, very long record
Chesapeake Capital (Jerry Parker)Long-term trend-followingParker was one of the original "Turtle Traders"
Mulvaney CapitalConcentrated long-term trendFamous for big years in big trends
Renaissance TechnologiesStatistical pattern-findingPrice/data patterns rather than company fundamentals (see Jim Simons)

How they're doing: trend-followers have had a strong 2026. The SG CTA Index was up 15.7% through Q3, ahead of the S&P 500's 11.7% (Alpha Maven), helped by big trends in oil and rates.

An important point: systematic funds rarely use Fibonacci. They rely on moving averages and breakouts. Fibonacci is mostly used by discretionary chart traders — the people below.
